 [Report] "Fierce competition with other channels"… K-Beauty zones in every London beauty store
 By Ha Sumin 
 1:00 p.m. 
 Nov 1, 2026 
 [Visiting the front lines of K-Initiative riding the 2026 K-Wave] Amorepacific
 K-brand products have permeated the daily lives of people around the world. The goal of our consumer goods companies goes beyond expanding exports. They build factories at local bases, establish innovative logistics systems, and analyze local purchasing data to unveil specialized products. They also pursue localization efforts. All of this is for sustainable growth. As we enter the era of "K-Brand 3.0," where businesses have expanded through overseas expansion (K-Brand 1.0) and business development (K-Brand 2.0), and are now entering a stage of integration with local ecosystems, we examine the activities of our companies deploying fierce survival strategies in global battlegrounds.
 On the 10th (local time), customers select K-skincare products at a Beauty Channel store in White City Westfield, London, UK. /Photo=Reporter Ha Su-min 
 "May I ask what you are photographing for? Competition with other channels is extremely intense these days." 
 When photos were taken at a beauty store in London, UK on the 10th of last month (local time), an employee rushed over to first ask about the purpose of the shooting. Upon explaining that we were accompanied by a brand company official, the response was, "Then it is fine." It was a moment that offered a glimpse into the competitive atmosphere of the UK beauty market, where each store deliberates on which brands to stock and which products to place prominently.
 Amidst fierce channel competition, London beauty stores shared one common feature: the "K-Beauty Zone," an area dedicated to Korean cosmetics. While the nature of the stores varied from premium beauty concept stores to drugstores and global cosmetics specialty shops, all introduced Korean cosmetics in a separate section. This shows that K-Beauty has established itself as a product category attracting attention from local distributors, surpassing the popularity of individual products.
 At Space NK near Oxford Circus in London, Laneige occupied the center of the store while various premium beauty brands filled the shelves. Laneige was also included in Space NK's Christmas advent calendar. K-Beauty has been incorporated into a product configuration where customers open one product per day while waiting for Christmas.
 Amorepacific's derma skincare brand, Aestura, could also be found in stores. Recently stocked, Aestura was placed in the area gathering skin care products. Laneige, which emphasizes moisturizing, and Aestura, specialized in skin barrier management, meet consumers through different product categories. Even for brands from the same company, their location within the store varied depending on product characteristics and consumer demand.
 On the 12th (local time), customers select K-skincare products at a local beauty channel store in London, UK. /Photo=Reporter Ha Su-min 
 Dedicated K-Beauty zones were also confirmed at the Boots store in Battersea Power Station, London, and the Sephora UK store in White City Westfield. Boots is a drugstore that handles a wide range of cosmetics and household goods. Sephora is a specialty store where customers can compare and purchase various global beauty brands in one place. All three stores, which differ in customer base and product composition, were introducing Korean cosmetics collectively.
 In the UK beauty distribution market, how products are selected and displayed is as important as securing shelf space itself. As diverse brands compete, distributors compose their merchandise according to the store's character and customer demand. From the brand's perspective, display location and product composition determine the consumer's first impression. The dedicated K-Beauty zone shows a shift in local distribution that introduces multiple brands together while treating Korean cosmetics as a single product category.
 Amorepacific utilizes offline distribution networks such as Selfridges and John Lewis, in addition to Space NK, Boots, and Sephora. Online, it has expanded sales touchpoints through Lookfantastic, ASOS, and Amazon. The growth momentum of its European business is also continuing. Amorepacific's revenue in the Europe, Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) region increased from 51.8 billion won in 2023 to 241 billion won in 2025. EMEA's share of total revenue also rose from 3.7% to 5.7% over the same period.
 Expanding brand positions within local distribution networks is a challenge. Laneige differentiates itself by emphasizing moisturizing care and product experience, while Aestura differentiates as a derma skincare brand specialized in skin barrier management. COSRX targets demand for ingredient- and efficacy-focused skincare. While meeting consumers under the common name of K-Beauty, they are conveying each brand's strengths.
